Definition: from G5311; to elevate (literally or figuratively):--exalt, lift up.
BiblicalUsage: hypsóō turns up where the Bible says to exalt, to lift up. In Matthew 11:23, the text says "which art exalted unto heaven." In Luke 1:52, the text says "and exalted them of low degree."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading hypsóō this way, I believe glory is the weight of who God is, and it is the end of everything He does. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Pentecost; The Bronze Serpent; Mary Visits Elizabeth
